requirements.objective: Provide an auditable record of meeting eligibility, proxy authority and voting outcomes for a housing cooperative pilot covering one meeting, up to 2,000 memberships, 20 ordinary motions and one single-seat director election.

requirements.normalized: Limit the pilot to one meeting, up to 2,000 memberships, 20 ordinary motions and one single-seat director election.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should cover the stated pilot capacity and contest types.

requirements.normalized: Give each eligible membership one vote per contest regardless of its number of owners, and take eligibility explicitly from the approved membership roll without inferring it from arrears or ownership documents.
acceptance_implications: Multiple owners must not multiply a membership's votes.
Eligibility must follow the roll's explicit eligibility value.

requirements.normalized: Exclude dues collection, ownership-dispute resolution, campaigning, member messaging and bylaw changes.
acceptance_implications: The pilot scope must not include these activities.

requirements.normalized: Allow a secretary to preview and accept a membership roll containing meeting_id, membership_id, eligible and source_reference. Reject the entire roll for missing fields, repeated membership identifiers or invalid eligibility values, with row-level reasons and no changes.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should exercise preview, valid acceptance and atomic rejection for each stated error.
A rejected roll must leave existing data unchanged.

requirements.normalized: Accepting a replacement roll must create a new version and retain the previous version.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should confirm that replacing a roll preserves the previous version.

requirements.normalized: Require the meeting chair to freeze a roll version before counting, fixing the eligible-membership denominator. Later corrections require a reasoned amendment and a new freeze, making affected draft results stale without overwriting certified history.
acceptance_implications: Counting must require a frozen roll version.
Proposed verification should confirm that a correction requires a reason and new freeze, invalidates affected drafts and preserves certified history.

requirements.normalized: A proxy grant must identify the represented membership, holder membership, valid_from, valid_until and evidence reference. Both memberships must be distinct and eligible on the frozen roll. Use UTC timestamps and half-open validity intervals with the end later than the start.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should reject self-proxies, ineligible parties and nonpositive intervals.
A grant covers its start timestamp and excludes its end timestamp.

requirements.normalized: Disallow overlapping grants from a represented membership to different holders, limit a holder to two other represented memberships at any instant, exclude the holder's own vote from that limit and prohibit onward delegation of proxy authority.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should evaluate overlapping intervals and simultaneous holder capacity.
A holder voting for itself and two represented memberships contributes three membership votes.
Proxy authority must not support an onward delegation chain.

requirements.normalized: A revocation must shorten a grant's validity and preserve actor, time and reason without invalidating a ballot validly cast before the revocation took effect.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should compare ballots cast before and at or after the effective revocation boundary.
The revocation audit record must retain actor, time and reason.

requirements.normalized: Keep local credential validation and synthetic ballot parsing, validation and selection independent of external-provider access. Ordinary-motion credentials, selection and counting must proceed while director proxy policy remains unresolved.
acceptance_implications: Proposed local verification must be possible without provider credentials or a connection.
Director-policy and live-exchange blockers must not disable ordinary-motion processing.

requirements.normalized: Use the voting window from 14:00 UTC inclusive to 16:00 UTC exclusive on the configured meeting date.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should include ballots at opening, immediately before closing and exactly at closing.
A ballot at 16:00 UTC is invalid.

requirements.normalized: Allow a secretary to preview local ballot files containing ballot_id, contest_id, represented_membership_id, casting_membership_id, cast_at and choice. Ordinary choices are YES, NO or ABSTAIN; director choices are a declared candidate identifier or ABSTAIN. Reject an entire file containing malformed rows, unknown contests or undeclared choices, with row-level reasons and no changes.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should cover both contest types and every stated file-rejection condition.
Rejected files must make no changes.

requirements.normalized: Treat an identical ballot identifier and content as a no-op and reject changed content under an existing ballot identifier.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should confirm that identical reimports do not create additional ballot evidence or votes.
Changed content must not overwrite the original ballot.
The transaction scope for a changed-content collision in a mixed file requires clarification.

requirements.normalized: Preserve every imported ballot and its validation explanation. Retain ballots outside the voting window or from ineligible memberships as invalid evidence and never count them.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should distinguish structurally rejected files from imported ballots retained as invalid evidence.
Invalid retained ballots must have explanations and contribute no counted votes.

requirements.normalized: Classify a ballot as direct when represented and casting membership identifiers match. A proxy ballot requires the casting holder's grant for the represented membership to cover cast_at.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should check the holder, represented membership and grant interval against cast_at.
A missing or noncovering grant must not produce a valid proxy vote.

requirements.normalized: For each membership and contest, select the latest valid direct ballot ahead of every proxy ballot. Only when no valid direct ballot exists, select the latest valid proxy ballot.
acceptance_implications: A valid direct YES at 14:10 must defeat a valid proxy NO at 15:00 for the same membership and motion.
Proposed verification should confirm that an invalid direct ballot does not displace a valid proxy ballot.

requirements.normalized: Conflicting choices at the latest timestamp within the selected ballot class leave the membership's contest vote unresolved. Do not resolve the conflict by import order or ballot identifier, and block certification of that contest.
acceptance_implications: Two different latest direct choices at 15:30 must remain unresolved.
Proposed verification should permute import order and ballot identifiers without resolving the conflict.
An affected contest must not certify while an unresolved selected vote remains.

requirements.normalized: For each ordinary motion, require quorum of ceiling(0.60 × frozen-roll eligible memberships), counting represented memberships with selected valid ballots. ABSTAIN counts toward quorum; eligible nonvoters remain in the denominator.
acceptance_implications: With 101 eligible memberships, quorum must be 61.
Sixty represented memberships must produce NO QUORUM.
A holder casting its own vote and two valid represented votes contributes three memberships toward quorum.

requirements.normalized: With quorum, an ordinary motion passes only when YES exceeds NO. Exclude ABSTAIN from the decision denominator. A tie or zero YES and zero NO does not pass. Without quorum, report NO QUORUM rather than a failed motion.
acceptance_implications: With 101 eligible memberships, YES=30, NO=30 and ABSTAIN=1 meet quorum but do not pass.
YES=31, NO=29 and ABSTAIN=1 pass.
Proposed verification should include an all-abstention quorum and a below-quorum majority.

requirements.normalized: Ordinary-motion results must show the frozen-roll version, eligible count, quorum requirement, represented count and YES, NO and ABSTAIN totals.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should compare every displayed result field with the referenced roll and selected votes.

requirements.normalized: The signed election rules require proxy votes to be permitted in the director election; this mandatory statement conflicts with the adopted meeting resolution and cannot be adopted as the operative policy without resolution.
acceptance_implications: No acceptance expectation may assume that this statement takes precedence over the conflicting resolution.
external_dependencies: Election-officer resolution of the director proxy-policy contradiction.

requirements.normalized: The current adopted meeting resolution requires proxy votes to be prohibited in the director election; this mandatory statement conflicts with the signed election rules and cannot be adopted as the operative policy without resolution.
acceptance_implications: No acceptance expectation may assume that this resolution takes precedence over the conflicting election rules.
external_dependencies: Election-officer resolution of the director proxy-policy contradiction.

requirements.normalized: Require election-officer resolution of the director proxy-policy contradiction. Until resolution, retain structurally valid director proxy ballots as unresolved evidence without silently counting or discarding them, block director certification and assert no director winner.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should confirm evidence retention, the director certification hold and absence of an asserted director winner.
The unresolved-policy safeguards can be implemented before a policy ruling exists.
Ordinary-motion processing must remain available.
external_dependencies: Election-officer ruling is needed to release the director-policy hold.

requirements.normalized: After director proxy policy is resolved, determine the single-seat winner by the highest number of selected valid candidate votes, excluding ABSTAIN. Equal highest totals or no candidate votes produce NO WINNER and require a separately convened election instead of an automatic draw.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should cover a unique highest total, tied highest totals and no candidate votes.
Actual director winner acceptance remains conditional on the proxy-policy ruling.
A NO WINNER outcome must not trigger an automatic draw.

requirements.normalized: Initial motion results may be ordered by agenda order or title; presentation order must not change outcomes. Any initial ordering choice must be labeled as a reversible assumption rather than customer approval of that choice.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should confirm identical selected votes and outcomes under either ordering.
The chosen default must be identified as an unapproved reversible assumption.

requirements.normalized: Allow an election officer to prepare a versioned result package and certify an unblocked contest only against the current frozen roll, credentials and ballot evidence. Reject certification of stale calculations.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should change each calculation input and confirm rejection of stale certification.
Blocked contests must not certify.
An independently unblocked ordinary motion may certify while director policy remains unresolved.

requirements.normalized: Changes affecting a certified result require a separately reviewed amendment linked to the original certified package. Never overwrite the certified package or certified history.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should confirm that amended results retain the original package, review evidence and linkage.

requirements.normalized: Provide a review overview showing credential violations, invalid ballots, unresolved selections, quorum outcomes, stale calculations and publication status with supporting references.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should confirm that each required review category appears with references supporting its status.

requirements.normalized: Public results must contain aggregate totals only. Retained audit evidence must support authorized review without exposing individual choices publicly.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should inspect public result representations for individual choices or individual ballot evidence.
Authorized evidence review must remain available.

requirements.normalized: Enforce role permissions beyond screen visibility: viewers read aggregates; secretaries maintain rolls, credentials and ballot intake; election officers inspect individual evidence, resolve director policy and certify results; only the meeting chair freezes rolls and authorizes publication. Restrict access to individual choices.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should exercise direct access attempts as well as visible controls.
Unauthorized roles must be denied privileged operations and individual-choice access.
These permission requirements do not grant any present operational authorization.

requirements.normalized: Support trusted live ballot-export intake from the external voting provider once its connection, authentication, meeting permissions, ballot authenticity evidence and authoritative timestamp semantics are established.
acceptance_implications: Trusted live intake cannot be accepted using synthetic files alone.
Provider contract details, credentials and authorized access must be established before live exchange.
Local synthetic intake remains independently available.
external_dependencies: Provider meeting permissions and operational credentials.
Ballot authenticity evidence and authoritative timestamp semantics.
external_effects: Authenticated requests to the external voting provider for ballot exports.

requirements.normalized: Support publication of certified aggregate results through the external voting provider to the member portal only after the provider publication contract and required operation authorizations are established.
acceptance_implications: Live publication requires established endpoint, authentication, meeting permissions, publication schema and duplicate-publication behavior.
No supplied source constitutes permission to execute a publication.
Provider gaps must not block local calculation, review or preparation of certified packages.
external_dependencies: Provider endpoint, authentication and meeting permissions.
Provider publication schema and duplicate-publication behavior.
Operational credentials and exact-package publication authorization.
external_effects: Publication of certified aggregate results to the member portal through the provider.

requirements.normalized: Before each publication attempt, require separate meeting-chair authorization identifying the exact certified package version, meeting and contest set. Changed results invalidate that authorization. Certification alone is insufficient. Recheck currency and authorization immediately before sending.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should reject missing, mismatched or invalidated authorization.
Proposed verification should change results after authorization and confirm that sending is blocked.
The brief itself grants no execution permission.
external_dependencies: Meeting-chair authorization is required for an actual publication attempt.

requirements.normalized: Preserve publication outcomes as rejected, accepted for processing, published or unknown, linking each outcome to the attempted package and authorization. Do not treat acceptance for processing as publication.
acceptance_implications: Proposed local verification should exercise all four outcomes and their package and authorization links.
An accepted-for-processing response must not display or record a published outcome.

requirements.normalized: Treat a publication timeout as an unknown outcome, prohibit automatic retry and require documented outcome resolution before another attempt.
acceptance_implications: Proposed local verification should simulate a timeout and confirm an unknown outcome with no automatic resend.
Another attempt must remain blocked until outcome resolution is documented and publication authorization is rechecked.
The local hold and documentation rule can be verified independently of a live provider.

requirements.normalized: Persist rolls, grants, ballots, explanations, certified versions and authorization history across restart, preserving identical selected votes and totals.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification should compare retained records, selected votes and totals before and after restart.
Restart must preserve certified versions and authorization history.

requirements.normalized: Describe verification as proposed work. No implementation, executed tests or live-provider evidence is supplied. Any local-storage, preview-layout or initial-ordering assumption must be explicitly labeled reversible and not customer-approved.
acceptance_implications: Analysis and delivery descriptions must not claim executed tests, implemented behavior or verified live exchange.
Proposed technical choices must remain distinguishable from customer requirements.

issues.description: Two mandatory sources respectively permit and prohibit director-election proxy votes, and no precedence ruling exists. The operative director policy, winner determination and release of director certification remain blocked.
issues.question: What director proxy policy does the cooperative's election officer formally resolve as operative?
issues.rationale: The ruling changes which director votes may count and therefore the winner. Evidence retention and certification safeguards can proceed, as can all ordinary-motion credentials, selection and counting.

issues.description: Trusted live ballot intake lacks the provider endpoint, authentication, meeting permissions, credentials, ballot authenticity evidence and authoritative timestamp semantics.
issues.question: What provider contract, access credentials, meeting permissions, authenticity evidence and timestamp semantics govern live ballot exports?
issues.rationale: These determine whether live ballots can be acquired and trusted. They do not block local synthetic parsing, credential validation, selection or ordinary counting.

issues.description: Live publication lacks the provider endpoint, authentication, meeting permissions, publication schema and duplicate-publication behavior. The provider-specific means of determining an unknown attempt's outcome is also unspecified.
issues.question: What publication contract and documented outcome-resolution procedure establish whether an attempt published results and whether a subsequent attempt is safe?
issues.rationale: These details affect live publication and resolution of uncertain external effects. Local package preparation, authorization enforcement, outcome recording and timeout holds remain implementable.

issues.description: External accounts, credentials and operation authorizations are absent. No meeting-chair authorization identifies an exact certified package version, meeting and contest set for publication.
issues.question: Before any live operation, what authorized provider access applies, and, before publication, where is the meeting chair's authorization for the exact certified package version, meeting and contest set?
issues.rationale: An integration requirement or certification does not authorize external execution. Missing authorization blocks actual live operations, without blocking local implementation or synthetic verification of permission checks.

issues.description: Changed content under an existing ballot identifier must be rejected, but the source does not explicitly state whether that collision rejects an otherwise valid mixed file atomically or only the conflicting ballot.
issues.question: If a file contains both new valid ballots and changed content under an existing ballot identifier, must the entire file be rejected with no changes?
issues.rationale: The answer changes import transaction boundaries and persisted evidence. Only mixed-file collision handling is blocked; the stated malformed-file rejection rules, identical reimport behavior and other local validation remain clear.

issues.description: Users disagree about agenda order versus title order for initial motion results, but either is explicitly acceptable.
issues.question: Should the reversible initial presentation default use agenda order or title order?
issues.rationale: The choice affects presentation only and must not affect outcomes. A labeled reversible assumption permits continued work.

issues.description: The actual meeting date, contest identifiers and declared candidate identifiers are not supplied.
issues.question: What meeting date, contest catalog and declared candidate identifiers will configure the pilot meeting?
issues.rationale: These are required configuration values for actual meeting processing. Explicitly synthetic values can support proposed local verification without selecting real meeting facts or blocking configurable implementation.

assumptions.statement: For local planning, use a replaceable local persistent store; no particular storage engine is selected or customer-approved.
assumptions.rationale: The source explicitly permits reversible local-storage assumptions while requiring restart durability.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The storage adapter and persistence verification may change; retained evidence and deterministic restart behavior must still satisfy REQ-2c64c88852c8.

assumptions.statement: Use a reversible tabular preview showing submitted rows and their validation reasons for local planning.
assumptions.rationale: The source requires preview and row-level reasons while explicitly allowing a reversible preview-layout assumption.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The preview presentation may need revision without changing validation or atomic rejection rules.

assumptions.statement: Use title order as the reversible initial motion-results presentation default.
assumptions.rationale: Either title order or agenda order is explicitly acceptable, and the source permits a labeled reversible ordering assumption.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Change the presentation default to agenda order without changing selected votes, totals or outcomes.

Purpose and boundaries
source_segments.text: A housing cooperative needs an auditable record of meeting eligibility, proxy authority and voting outcomes. The pilot covers one meeting, up to 2,000 memberships, 20 ordinary motions and one single-seat director election. Each eligible membership has one vote per contest, regardless of how many people own it. The approved membership roll explicitly states eligibility; the service does not infer it from arrears or ownership documents. The service does not collect dues, resolve ownership disputes, conduct campaigning, send member messages or change bylaws. Synthetic rolls, proxy grants and ballots are available; external credentials, accounts and operation authorizations are absent.

AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Eligibility and proxy credentials
source_segments.text: A secretary can preview and accept a membership roll containing meeting_id, membership_id, eligible and source_reference. Missing fields, repeated membership identifiers or invalid eligibility values reject the entire roll with row-level reasons and no changes. Accepting a replacement creates a new roll version and retains the previous one. The meeting chair must freeze a roll version before counting; that version fixes the eligible-membership denominator. Later corrections require a reasoned amendment and a new freeze, making affected draft results stale without overwriting certified history.

heading_path: AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Eligibility and proxy credentials
source_segments.text: A proxy grant names the represented membership, its holder membership, valid_from, valid_until and evidence reference. Both memberships must be eligible on the frozen roll and must differ. Use UTC timestamps and half-open validity intervals; end must be later than start. A membership cannot have overlapping grants to different holders. A holder may represent at most two other memberships at any instant; its own vote does not consume that limit. Proxy authority cannot be delegated onward. A revocation shortens the grant's validity and preserves actor, time and reason; it does not invalidate a ballot validly cast before the revocation took effect. Credential validation can be planned locally before a voting-provider connection exists.

Ballot evidence and selection
source_segments.text: Voting opens at 14:00 UTC and closes at 16:00 UTC on the configured meeting date. Opening is inclusive and closing exclusive. A secretary can preview a local ballot file containing ballot_id, contest_id, represented_membership_id, casting_membership_id, cast_at and choice. Ordinary choices are YES, NO or ABSTAIN; director choices are one declared candidate identifier or ABSTAIN. Reject a whole file for malformed rows, unknown contests or undeclared choices, with row-level reasons and no changes. An identical ballot identifier and content is a no-op; changed content under that identifier is rejected. Preserve every imported ballot and its validation explanation.

heading_path: AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Ballot evidence and selection
source_segments.text: Ballots outside the voting window or from ineligible memberships are retained as invalid evidence and never counted. A direct ballot has matching represented and casting identifiers. A proxy ballot requires the holder's grant to cover cast_at. For each membership and contest, the latest valid direct ballot takes precedence over every proxy ballot, even a later proxy ballot. If there is no valid direct ballot, use the latest valid proxy ballot. Conflicting choices with the same latest timestamp leave that membership's contest vote unresolved; do not break the tie by import order or ballot identifier. An unresolved selected vote blocks certification of that contest. Ballot parsing, validation and selection can be planned with synthetic files independently of external access.

heading_path: AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Ordinary motions
AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Ordinary motions
source_segments.text: For each motion, quorum requires selected valid ballots from at least 60% of eligible memberships on the frozen roll, rounded upward to a whole membership. Count represented memberships, not people attending or proxy holders. ABSTAIN counts toward quorum but not the decision denominator. With quorum, a motion passes only when YES is strictly greater than NO; a tie or zero YES and zero NO does not pass. Without quorum, report NO QUORUM rather than a failed motion. A nonvoting eligible membership remains in the quorum denominator. Results must show the frozen-roll version, eligible count, quorum requirement, represented count and YES, NO and ABSTAIN totals.

heading_path: AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Director-election contradiction
AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Director-election contradiction
source_segments.text: The signed election rules state “proxy votes are permitted in the director election.” The current adopted meeting resolution states “proxy votes are prohibited in the director election.” Both are mandatory and no precedence ruling exists. The cooperative's election officer must resolve this contradiction. Retain structurally valid director proxy ballots as unresolved evidence; do not silently count or discard them. Director certification is blocked until resolution. Ordinary-motion credentials, selection and counting must proceed meanwhile. Once proxy policy is resolved, the director winner is the candidate with the most selected valid votes, excluding ABSTAIN; equal highest totals or no candidate votes produce NO WINNER and require a separately convened election, not an automatic draw. Users disagree whether results should initially list motions by agenda order or title; either presentation is acceptable and must not change outcomes.

AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Review, privacy and publication
source_segments.text: An election officer can prepare a versioned result package and certify an unblocked contest only against the current frozen roll, credentials and ballot evidence. Certification must reject stale calculations. Changes affecting a certified result require a separately reviewed amendment linked to the original; never overwrite the certified package. The review overview must show credential violations, invalid ballots, unresolved selections, quorum outcomes, stale calculations and publication status with supporting references. Public results contain aggregate totals only. Viewers can read aggregates; secretaries maintain rolls, credentials and ballot intake; election officers inspect individual evidence, resolve director policy and certify results; only the meeting chair freezes rolls and authorizes publication. Enforce permissions beyond screen visibility, including restrictions on access to individual choices. Retained audit evidence must support authorized review without exposing individual choices publicly.

heading_path: AssemblyCount: cooperative meeting credentials and voting
Review, privacy and publication
source_segments.text: The external voting provider is expected to supply ballot exports and publish certified results to the member portal. Its endpoint, authentication, meeting permissions, ballot authenticity evidence, authoritative timestamp semantics, publication schema and duplicate-publication behavior are unknown. These block trusted live exchange, not local synthetic validation or ordinary counting. Before a publication attempt, the meeting chair must separately authorize the exact certified package version, meeting and contest set. This brief grants no execution permission. Changed results invalidate that authorization; certification alone is not publication permission. Recheck currency and authorization immediately before sending. Preserve rejected, accepted for processing, published and unknown outcomes; acceptance is not publication. A timeout is unknown and requires documented outcome resolution before another attempt, without automatic retry. Link outcomes to the attempted package and authorization.

source_segments.text: With 101 eligible memberships, quorum is 61. Totals YES=30, NO=30 and ABSTAIN=1 meet quorum but do not pass; YES=31, NO=29 and ABSTAIN=1 pass. Sixty represented memberships produce NO QUORUM. One holder voting for itself and two represented memberships contributes three membership votes, not one. A valid direct YES at 14:10 defeats a valid proxy NO at 15:00 for the same membership and motion. A ballot at 16:00 is invalid. Two different latest direct choices both timestamped 15:30 remain unresolved. No director winner is asserted before proxy-policy resolution.

Local storage, preview layout and initial result ordering may use explicitly labeled reversible assumptions; none is customer approval. planning_objective: Create one implementation-independent technical contract per increment with the same task ID. Include source-based business rules, preconditions/data structures/validation/error behavior and objective acceptance criteria. Each contract must cover all its increment requirement IDs AND global requirement IDs. Every contract needs normal, invalid and boundary criteria; external operations also need permission checks and future real external verification. All criteria state=proposed. Each criterion must specify concrete given/action/expected observable results. Preserve source exclusions. Do not invent business-rule precedence or resolve blockers. For blocked business behavior specify safe fail-closed behavior while unresolved and list issue IDs; final behavior remains pending clarification. Existing increment inputs/outputs/interfaces/permissions/effects stay authoritative and apply to the contract. Keep responses concise enough for existing bounded context; no tests have been generated, protected or run for the planned product.
